articles.title: Why we should all get used to high household energy bills
articles.summary: The government is under pressure to support billpayers when domestic energy prices predicted to rise further.
articles.body:
Energy bills may have been a long way from our minds through the sweltering summer.

Clothes on a washing line have been drying in minutes. Cold showers have been more tempting than hot ones.

But the latest news and forecasts on gas prices will bring a renewed sense of worry and urgency to families, as well as government ministers.

Energy prices will rise by nearly 4% for millions of households in October. Even more striking is a prediction from the respected consultancy Cornwall Insight of a further 9% increase at the peak of winter in January.

With ongoing volatility in the wholesale gas market sparked by events in the Gulf region, the energy sector says high prices are here to stay.

EDF suggests bills will remain "stubbornly high" at their current level at least until the end of the decade.

High bills have, and continue to, bite. Energy prices have been central to the cost-of-living squeeze.

The typical household's dual-fuel bill is now 70% higher than it was at the start of 2021, before Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

That amounts to around £600 more each year than pre-crisis levels, according to industry body Energy UK.

Inevitably, more and more people have been unable to pay. Unpaid energy debt of more than three months is now at a record high, according to regulator Ofgem.

Suppliers, who chart debt levels for missed payments of a month or more, estimate total unpaid bills and charges to have reached £6bn. By the end of the year, they expect that to rise to £7bn.

The average household in debt, without a repayment plan, owes more than the typical annual bill.

And even if you are not in debt, you pay. Covering the cost of debt already adds about £60 to the average annual bill. Consultancy Baringa says everyone could, on average, be paying £100 to cover the cost of unpaid debts by the end of the year.

So, pressure on the government to help those most in need will only intensify.

Ofgem has a proposed debt relief scheme on the table, and campaigners keep telling them to get on with it, urging the government as to provide funding for it to be implemented.

Charities and the industry also want ministers to introduce a discounted tariff for those who need it most - based on benefits, health and income data.

Energy UK says a targeted plan would cost £1.9bn. That would be much cheaper than the £40bn commitment to protect everyone's bills after Russia invaded Ukraine.

But, who would pay? It could go on everyone else's bills. Or ministers could opt to raise taxes, borrow the money, or cancel spending elsewhere - all of which are tricky political choices.

Those who can have cut back on their energy use to reduce bills in recent years. Thermostats up and down the country have not been set as high as before. Batch cooking is more common.

So much so that Ofgem's official calculations for typical energy consumption were lowered again in July (to 9,500 kWh of gas and 2,500 kWh of electricity a year).

Millions have shifted onto fixed tariffs, with 35% of billpayers on such a deal.

So, many can justifiably say they have done their bit. Others who are older or who have health conditions might not have the luxury of lowering their energy use.

So, community warm hubs have become popular. Some became cold hubs during the hot summer so people could make use of the air con.

The heatwave has reduced the amount of energy stored across Europe, which needs to be restocked, piling more pressure on prices.

Add to that the huge cost of upgrading the UK's electricity network and you can see why there are predictions of longstanding high energy bills - irrespective of whether a lasting peace in the Iran war brings down the international price of wholesale gas.

In the long-term, the government and Ofgem wants to shift the country away from our reliance on gas, with its volatile international pricing.

Expect lots of fanfare over the sale, for the first time in the UK, of plug-in solar panels.

In the short-term ministers - and the new prime minister - say they are helping where they can, and promising that there is "more to do".

VAT will be cut on electricity bills in October. It means the price of electricity will fall, but that's been more than outstripped by an 8% rise in the price of gas.

In the last Budget, then-Chancellor Rachel Reeves cut some so-called policy costs and shifted some onto general taxation instead.

Ministers may be tempted to do more of that, but could face be criticised for simply shifting the burden off bills and onto taxes.

So, the options are limited. The new chancellor, John Healey, has choices to make - with lots of calls for help but with limited room for manoeuvre in the public finances.

All eyes will be on his first Budget, which comes soon after those higher autumn energy bills kick in.

What will the energy cap changes mean for my bills?

articles.title: Over 100 Indians missing after flash floods hit Nepal - what we know so far
articles.summary: South Asia News: Over 100 Indians were reported missing after a massive flash flood swept through Nepalâs Rasuwa district near the Tibet border on Wednesday, killing a.
articles.body: Over 100 Indians were reported missing after a massive flash flood swept through Nepalâs Rasuwa district near the Tibet border on Wednesday, killing at least eight people and causing widespread damage to settlements and infrastructure.The sudden surge in the Bhote Koshi River struck the Rasuwagadhi-Timure area at around 9 am local time, affecting Rasuwa as well as parts of neighbouring Nuwakot and Dhading districts.The flooding washed away vehicles, goods, bridges and other infrastructure, while several hydropower projects were also damaged.105 Indians missingAccording to a preliminary list compiled by the Nepal Tourism Board, 384 travellers, including 291 foreign nationals and 93 Nepali nationals, have been reported missing following the flash flood.Of the foreign nationals, 105 are from India. The list also includes travellers from Australia, the Netherlands, the US, Malaysia, the UK and South Africa, while the nationalities of some others are yet to be confirmed.The Tourism Board said the list is preliminary and is being verified in coordination with travel agencies, guides, local authorities and security agencies. It urged travellers and their families not to draw conclusions until the verification process is complete.Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims among those missingA large number of those out of contact are believed to be pilgrims travelling to Tibet for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra.Bashu Kumar Adhikari, managing director of Kathmandu-based Touch Kailash Travels & Tours, said 390 pilgrims, including 93 Nepalis, were scheduled to cross the border on Wednesday.âExcept for a few, we have not been able to establish contact with the pilgrims as of 3pm,â Adhikari said, according to The Kathmandu Post.Sagar Pandey, president of the Trekking Agenciesâ Association of Nepal, said efforts were underway to contact the pilgrims and assess their condition.Several dead, rescue operations under wayAt least eight people have been confirmed dead, while more than 25 people had been rescued by Wednesday afternoon, according to Nepal Army officials cited by local media.Four bodies were recovered from Bidur Municipality in Nuwakot and were found near the Trishuli river, according to police.The Nepal Army, Armed Police Force and Nepal Police have been mobilised for search-and-rescue operations. As many as 14 helicopters have been deployed, while drones and sniffer dogs are also being used to locate missing people.The Nepal Army said six people were rescued from Syafrubesi, two from Mailung and four from Dhunche in Rasuwa. It has also set up a treatment centre at the Military Training Centre No 1 in Trishuli to provide emergency medical care.Four Armed Police Force personnel were initially reported missing from Rasuwa, while another report said nine personnel stationed at Timure, near the Nepal-China border, were unaccounted for.Flood alert issued along Gandak river in BiharThe Indian government has issued an advisory after a sudden rise in the water level of Nepalâs Trishuli river at Furke Khola, around 160 km from the Indian border, was reported amid suspected glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) activity near the Nepal-China border.The advisory said the flood wave is expected to move downstream into the Gandak river, with its intensity likely to reduce as it travels. Authorities in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh along the India-Nepal border have been asked to remain alert and closely monitor the situation.Authorities have also been advised to take necessary precautionary measures along the Gandak river. The gates of the Gandak Barrage should be operated in a manner that allows the anticipated floodwater to pass through safely.Amit Shah speaks to Bihar CMIn view of the potential flood threat in Bihar following heavy rainfall in Nepal, Union home minister Amit Shah spoke to Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary over the phone, according to news agency ANI.Shah assured the Bihar government of all possible assistance to deal with the situation. The National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) is also being mobilised to respond to any emergency.UP CM urges districts to remain vigilantUttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath expressed concern over the flood situation in Nepal and directed local authorities in vulnerable districts to remain alert.In a post on X, Yogi said, "The damage caused by the devastating floods in the Bhote Koshi River in Nepal's Rasuwa region is extremely worrying. Prayers to Lord Pashupatinath for the safety of all.""In view of the rise in water levels of the Gandak and Narayani rivers and the possibility of flooding in Uttar Pradesh's districts of Maharajganj and Kushinagar due to its impact, instructions have been issued to the local administration to remain fully vigilant and ensure necessary preparations," he added.What caused the flash flood?The exact cause of the sudden rise in the Bhote Koshi River remains unclear. Nepal's Department of Hydrology and Meteorology said the flooding was not caused by rainfall in Rasuwa.Officials are examining whether it could have been triggered by a glacial lake outburst flood, a landslide or another event on the Tibetan side of the border.Dinkar Kayastha, information officer at the department, said, âWe are still studying the matter, so the real cause is not yet known.âHe also warned that the risk from the Tibetan side had not disappeared and said, âwe need to be cautious.âOfficials have received informal information that a landslide may have temporarily blocked a river in Tibet before the swollen water burst through, but this has not yet been confirmed.Widespread damage, villages washed awayRasuwa has emerged as the worst-hit district, with Timure and Syafrubesi among the areas suffering extensive damage. Vehicles and goods stored at the customs premises were swept away and a recently built bridge was destroyed.Several settlements along the river have also been affected, including Syaphrubesi, Betrawati, Mailung, Salletar, Shantibazar, Pairebesi, Khalti Basti, Sole, Trishuli and Battar.A bridge in Gajuri in Dhading district was also washed away.The flash flood has severely affected Nepal's trade route with Tibet, with infrastructure at Rasuwagadhi, an important border crossing with China, damaged in the disaster.Hydropower projects damagedThe flooding has also hit Nepal's hydropower sector. According to the Independent Power Producers' Association Nepal, eight operational hydropower projects with a combined capacity of 354 MW and five projects under construction in Rasuwa and Nuwakot were damaged.Among the affected operational projects are the 111-MW Rasuwagadhi Hydropower Project, 78-MW Sanjen Khola Hydropower Project and 60-MW Upper Trishuli 3A project.Authorities issue safety warningNepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority has placed several downstream districts, including Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitawan and Gorkha, on high alert.Authorities have urged people living near the Trishuli and other rivers to stay away from riverbanks and move to safer areas. Tourists in the affected regions have also been advised to remain calm, stay informed and follow official safety instructions.As per local media, those needing emergency assistance can contact 1234, 1144 or the Tourist Police at 9851289445, or inform the nearest police or security post, local administration, travel agency, guide or tour operator.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Putin set to target UK': Britain on alert after PM Burnham's Ukraine visit, missile tech transfer
articles.summary: UK News: Britain has been warned to prepare for possible Russian retaliation after Prime Minister Andy Burnhamâs visit to Ukraine and the UKâs decision to shar.
articles.body: Britain has been warned to prepare for possible Russian retaliation after Prime Minister Andy Burnhamâs visit to Ukraine and the UKâs decision to share technology that could help Kyiv produce long-range missiles.Security sources cited by the Daily Mail have warned that Russia could mount a âdirect responseâ against Britain, amid concerns in Whitehall that Moscow may have underestimated Burnhamâs commitment to Ukraine.A senior source told the newspaper: âThe question being asked is, "How long do we keep poking the bear before it bites?"âThe warning comes after Britain agreed to hand Ukraine blueprints for British-made components used in the Storm Shadow cruise missile, allowing Kyiv to produce the long-range weapon domestically.Russia has reacted angrily to the move, with Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov saying on Monday that Britainâs involvement prevented âeven the slightest progressâ towards peace.Peskov also said the Russian military was gathering information on missile production sites in an apparent warning that such facilities could become targets.âBritain is involved in this war on the side of the Kyiv regime. Britain methodically and regularly adds fuel to the fire,â he said.Burnham hit back during his visit to Ukraine, asking: âWho started the fire? That's the question, isn't it?âHis trip to Kyiv was his first official international visit as prime minister, where he met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and chaired a meeting of the âcoalition of the willingâ, established by Britain and France to support Ukraine.The warnings of possible Russian action were reinforced by comments from former Russian deputy foreign minister Andrei Fedorov, who suggested Moscow could consider a âsemi-militaryâ response.Speaking to BBC Newsnight, Fedorov said there was pressure on Russian President Vladimir Putin âto undertake certain measures against UKâ.Asked what such a response could involve, he said: âIt could take the form of something might happen with enterprises, with factories which are producing drones for Ukraine.ââThey could be attacked not by Russia, but by from unknown sources.âThe comments come as Russia itself faces growing pressure from Ukrainian drone strikes, particularly against oil refineries and other critical infrastructure.President Vladimir Putin has issued a decree allowing the Russian state to temporarily take control of critical infrastructure if private owners fail to adequately protect facilities from Ukrainian drone attacks or rebuild damaged sites.The measure covers energy, industrial, communications, transport and logistics facilities, with Kremlin officials insisting it does not amount to widespread nationalisation.Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said businesses were often failing to pay sufficient attention to âanti-drone safetyâ, while Putin has called for stronger coordination between the military, security agencies and private companies.Ukraine has continued targeting Russian energy infrastructure, with its General Staff reporting strikes on the Afipsky and Novoshakhtinsk oil refineries.Burnham has nevertheless reaffirmed Britainâs support for Kyiv and said he plans to travel to the US next month with European leaders to press President Donald Trump on Ukraineâs defence needs.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Britain methodically and regularly adds fuel to the fire,â he said.Burnham hit back during his visit to Ukraine, asking: âWho started the fire? articles.title: How do navies hunt submarines? NATO's deadly game of detection beneath the waves
articles.summary: International News: NATO navies are once again turning their attention to one of the oldest and most difficult problems at sea, finding and neutralising an adversary's su.
articles.body: NATO navies are once again turning their attention to one of the oldest and most difficult problems at sea, finding and neutralising an adversary's submarines before they can strike. This week, Standing NATO Maritime Group One and Standing NATO Mine Countermeasures Group One joined Exercise Northern Viking 26 off the coast of Iceland. This was a US-led drill built around defending the Greenland-Iceland-United Kingdom Gap, one of the most strategically sensitive maritime corridors in the world. The waters between Greenland and Iceland, and between Iceland and Britain, have long served as the primary route through which Russian submarines would have to pass to threaten the North Atlantic. This makes the Greenland-Iceland-UK gap a natural chokepoint for anti-submarine operations since the Cold War.Hunting submarines, however, remains one of the most technically demanding forms of naval warfare. Submarines rely on stealth as their primary defence, and modern anti-submarine warfare has evolved into a layered contest fought largely through sound rather than sight. Passive sonar systems listen for the acoustic signature of a submarine inevitably generates. These acoustic signals are produced by the submarine's engines, propellers and other machinery.On the other hand, active sonar transmits a pulse and interprets its echo to pinpoint a target submarine's range and bearing. Networks of sonobuoys, dropped from patrol aircraft or helicopters, are spaced across a search area to detect and triangulate a submerged contact, while fixed hydrophone arrays on the seabed provide a persistent listening capability across critical corridors.Surface ships, submarines and maritime patrol aircraft all work in tandem, since no single platform can reliably hold a contact on its own, a principle that lies at the very heart of coordinated anti-submarine warfare doctrine. Exercises like Northern Viking underline a wider truth about anti-submarine warfare: detecting and holding a submarine at risk demands persistent coordination between different assets, advanced acoustic technology and an understanding of an operating environment that keeps changing.Since the end of the Second World War, India is the only country which has sunk a submerged submarine in conflict. During the 1971 war, Pakistani submarine PNS Ghazi was sunk by the destroyer INS Rajput outside Visakhapatnam harbour. The Ghazi had been sent to the Bay of Bengal to sink the aircraft carrier INS Vikrant. On the western naval front, Pakistani submarine had torpedoed and sunk the Indian frigate INS Khukri. Since the end of the Second World War many other ships have been sunk by submarines, such as the Argentinian cruiser ARA General Belgrano, which was sunk by a submarine during the Falkland War and the recent sinking of Iranian ship IRIS Dena near the Sri Lankan coast. As both submarines and anti-submarine systems are becoming more advanced, these changes are also making the act of 'killing' a submarine a more difficult task.

articles.title: 22,000 feet, -15Â°C: DRDO puts high-altitude combat parachute system to the test
articles.summary: Defence News: NEW DELHI: The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) on Wednesday announced that it had successfully tested the indigenously developed .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) on Wednesday announced that it had successfully tested the indigenously developed Military Combat Parachute System (MCPS) at the Nyoma-Mudh drop zone in Ladakh, one of the worldâs highest-altitude drop zones.According to the DRDO, test jumpers from its Aerial Delivery Research and Development Establishment (ADRDE), Agra, executed a jump from 22,000 feet above mean sea level at a temperature of â15Â°C.Wing Commander Rahul Jha, the chief test jumper, along with Master Warrant Officers RJ Singh and Vivek Tiwari, carried out the jump using the MCPS and its indigenous subsystems, including a para computer, oxygen system and jumpsuits. The parachute was deployed at 20,000 feet, followed by a safe landing at 13,700 feet.âThe successful trial demonstrated the efficacy, reliability and tactical employability of MCPS in extreme high-altitude conditions, reinforcing Indiaâs commitment to self-reliance in critical defence technologies,â it said.In October last year, Indian Air Force test jumpers successfully undertook a combat freefall jump from 32,000 feet using the MCPS. The feat made it the only parachute system currently in operational use by the Indian Armed Forces capable of deployment above 25,000 feet.The MCPS was developed by DRDOâs ADRDE and Defence Bioengineering and Electromedical Laboratory (DEBEL), Bengaluru. It incorporates enhanced tactical features such as a lower rate of descent and improved steering capabilities, enabling paratroopers to exit aircraft, deploy parachutes at predetermined altitudes, navigate accurately and land at designated zones.The system is also compatible with Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), reducing dependence on foreign navigation systems and making it less susceptible to external interference or denial of service.Its indigenous development is expected to reduce the armed forcesâ dependence on foreign equipment for maintenance and repairs, particularly during conflicts, while enabling faster turnaround for routine servicing.

articles.title: Bluefin and Visa launch unified card-present payment acceptance offering
articles.summary: Bluefin positioned the offering as a single deployment that brings together payment acceptance, security and device operations.
articles.body:
Bluefin has partnered with Visa to introduce a new card-present payment acceptance offering that integrates Bluefin's PCI-validated point-to-point encryption (P2PE) solution with Visa Acceptance Solutions.

Bluefin said the goal is to provide a "unified approach" to secure in-person payment acceptance for merchants, software providers and enterprise organisations.

It positioned the offering as a single deployment that brings together payment acceptance, security and device operations.

According to the announcement, the collaboration combines payment acceptance, PCI-validated security, tokenisation, device lifecycle management and enterprise payment infrastructure into one solution.

Bluefin is contributing its PCI-validated P2PE solution, secure decryption services, a certified payment application, terminal integration and P2PE Manager. Visa Acceptance Solutions will provide payment processing, tokenisation and global payment services.

The offering has launched with selected certified Ingenico Lane series POS devices.

It is designed for use across retail, hospitality, petroleum, healthcare, higher education and other enterprise environments. The architecture is intended to expand to additional certified device ecosystems over time.

Bluefin founder and chief strategy officer Ruston Miles said: "Enterprise organisations are no longer looking for individual payment technologies – they're looking for infrastructure that enables secure commerce across every channel.

"Our collaboration with Visa Acceptance Solutions reflects a shared vision that secure payment acceptance should be delivered as an integrated platform rather than a collection of independent components. By combining Visa Acceptance Solutions with Bluefin's card-present security infrastructure, we're helping organisations simplify deployment, reduce complexity, and build a stronger foundation for the future of enterprise commerce."

The solution will be available to merchants and software providers through Visa Acceptance Solutions, as well as Visa's global sales and partner channels.

"Bluefin and Visa launch unified card-present payment acceptance offering" was originally created and published by Electronic Payments International , a GlobalData owned brand.

articles.title: Miami Dolphins claim WR Ryan Miller off waivers from New York Giants
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins have claimed WR Ryan Miller off of waivers from the New York Giants, while another ex-Giant finds a new home.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins claimed wide receiver Ryan Miller off waivers from the New York Giants on Tuesday and waived Tahj Washington to open a roster spot.

The Giants released Miller on Monday as they began trimming the roster ahead of the final cut to 53. The 6-foot-2, 221-pound veteran joined New York in December 2025 after being claimed off waivers from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and re-signed as an exclusive rights free agent this offseason.

Miller, a 26-year-old former Furman standout, spent most of training camp with the third team and never appeared in a regular-season game for the Giants. Joint practices and the second preseason game against Miami gave the Dolphins familiarity with him. In that contest, he played 32 offensive snaps and six on special teams but was targeted once and finished without a catch.

Originally signed by Tampa Bay as an undrafted free agent in 2023, Miller appeared in 25 career games with 14 receptions for 162 yards and three touchdowns. He also recorded 14 special teams tackles during his time with the Buccaneers.

Elsewhere around the league, the Minnesota Vikings signed former Giants cornerback Tre Hawkins .

articles.title: Border Police rescue Israeli citizen after accidental entry into Area A near Ramallah
articles.summary: Entry to Area A, which is under the Palestinian Authority's civil and security control, is prohibited for Israelis. Border Police officers earlier this week...
articles.body:
Entry to Area A, which is under the Palestinian Authority's civil and security control, is prohibited for Israelis.

Border Police officers earlier this week rescued an Israeli citizen from Holon who had accidentally entered Area A of the West Bank near the Ramallah area after getting lost, Israel Police confirmed on Wednesday morning.

Upon receiving a report of the Israeli's entry, a Border Police team was sent out to search for the individual. Officers succeeded in contacting the Israeli over the phone before locating his vehicle and escorting him from the area.

On Sunday, soldiers from the Coordinator of the Government Activities in the Territories (COGAT)'s Civil Administration rescued three Israeli Jews who had separately entered Area A near Bethlehem, Jericho, and Ramallah.

One of the Israeli Jews was spotted near the village of Ein Arik, while armed. Officers from the Binyamin Region's Coordination and Liaison Administration worked to rescue him through coordination channels before transferring him to the IDF.

All three Israelis transferred to police for further handling

At the same time, the Civil Administration received a report about an Israeli Jewish woman who was seen walking through the city of Jericho in the Jordan Valley area, putting herself at risk.

Officers from the Jordan Valley Coordination and Liaison Administration acted quickly to rescue her. An initial investigation found that she had entered the Palestinian city intentionally.

In Bethlehem, an Israeli man who appeared to be suffering from mental distress was seen wandering the streets of the city. Local residents passed the information to security forces, and they quickly handed him over.

All three incidents were transferred to the Judea and Samaria District Police for further handling. The security establishment reiterated that entering Area A, which is under the control of the Palestinian Authority , is life-threatening and prohibited by law.

Avi Ashkenazi contributed to this report.

articles.title: Is Japan trying to build bridges with China after Taiwan spat?
articles.summary: Experts say Japanese lawmakers’ visit to Beijing signals an attempt by Japan to defrost its worst China rift in decades.
articles.body:
A delegation of Japanese politicians has travelled to Beijing this week in what observers say may be a bid to improve relations amid one of the worst rifts with China since the 1970s.

Among those in Japan’s delegation is Gaku Hashimoto, a member of the House of Representatives and Takaichi’s ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), alongside lawmakers from the opposition Komeito and Centrist Reform Alliance parties.

list 4 of 4 Trump threatens Iran’s partners: How do secondary sanctions work?

A diplomatic spat began in November last year when Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said if China were to attack Taiwan, it could “constitute a survival-threatening situation” for Japan that would justify the use of force.

Her comments angered Beijing. The next day, Xue Jian, China’s consul general in Osaka, wrote on X: “We have no choice but cut off that dirty neck that has been lunged at us without hesitation”, alongside an article about Takaichi. The post was later deleted.

Tokyo lodged a protest and asked for him to be disciplined; Beijing refused, and instead warned its citizens against travel to Japan alongside tightened trade restrictions.

This year, China ramped up tensions further, restricting exports of dual-use goods and rare earth materials which are necessary for building many high-tech products from smartphones to fighter jets.

So why is a Japanese delegation visiting China this week, and does Japan need China more than it may care to admit?

What historical grievances have there been between Japan and China?

Baked into this diplomatic spat are longstanding grievances between the two nations, traceable to the late 19th century.

Japan seized Taiwan from China in 1895 after winning the First Sino-Japanese War. It also occupied Manchuria – a historical region covering northeast China and parts of Russia – in 1931 and launched a full-scale invasion of China six years later, in a war that killed millions.

In 1945, Japan surrendered at the end of the World War II and the Republic of China (ROC) took control of Taiwan.

But in 1949, after losing the Chinese Civil War on the mainland, the ROC government relocated to Taipei, separating Taiwan from the rest of China ever since.

Beijing continues to claim Taiwan as its own territory, although the People’s Republic of China has never governed the island.

In 1972, the Joint Communique of the Government of Japan and the government of the People’s Republic of China was signed in Beijing. It normalised diplomatic relations between Japan and the PRC in mainland China, and Japan ended official relations with the ROC in Taiwan.

Against this historical backdrop, however, Beijing is likely to read any Japanese talk of military force as evidence of a return to wartime militarism, analysts say.

In November last year, Beijing imposed a ban on Japanese seafood following the comments regarding Taiwan by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. Then, in January, it restricted exports of dual-use goods and rare earth minerals for defence or military uses. Dual-use goods include software and technology with potential military or weapons-development applications.

In February, China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) placed 40 Japanese entities under restrictive trade measures relating to dual-use goods. It issued a separate “watch list” of 20 companies for which Chinese exporters must submit individual licence applications, risk assessment reports and written commitments that items will not be used for military or defensive capabilities.

China also issued travel warnings, discouraging its citizens from visiting Japan in an attempt to dent Japan’s vital tourism sector.

According to Shinichi Isa, a politician who has previously served at the Japanese embassy in China, bilateral ties have sunk to their lowest since the 1972 normalisation of relations.

In a post on X earlier this month, he wrote that officials had always remained in communication even during previous lows: “Now all channels between officials and ministries have been cut off.”

Beijing has also noted the severity of the situation, with its Foreign Ministry urging the Japanese government on Friday to take its diplomats’ efforts to repair relations “seriously” and to “take concrete actions” to normalise relations.

Dylan Loh, an associate professor in the Public Policy and Global Affairs programme at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore, told Al Jazeera that bilateral relations “have dropped to their lowest in recent memory; communications have ground to a halt, and there is even more mistrust at both the elite and people-to-people level”.

Can Japan afford to fall out with China?

Chinese arrivals in Japan slumped from 715,700 in October 2025 to 330,000 in December, with visitors from mainland China and Hong Kong normally making up about one-fifth of all visitors, according to a report by the Centre for Strategic and International Studies in February.

However, the report also found that the economic effect was minimal, partly due to a weak yen, as spending by tourists from Taiwan, South Korea, the United States, and Hong Kong offset the decline in Chinese arrivals.

The restrictions on exports of rare earth metals from China are more worrying, however.

China, which supplies about 80 percent of Japan’s rare earth imports, shipped no dysprosium or terbium oxide to Japan between November 2025 and May 2026. These elements are essential for the manufacture of high-performance magnets required for a variety of technological applications, fluorescent lights, and nuclear energy and defence components.

Motor vehicle manufacturers Nissan and Suzuki have reported supply disruptions as a result.

Masahiro Matsumura, professor of international politics and national security at St Andrew’s University in Osaka, told Al Jazeera that the squeeze will eventually be managed, but not quickly. “Over the medium and long run, the impact is likely managed through diversification, including rare earth issues, which is a focal point,” he said.

Japan has diversified the supply of some of these, he said, but still relies on China for others that matter, something he described as a “great headache” for the government and for Japanese high-tech firms.

Elsewhere, Beijing has been more careful.

“Beijing still welcomes Japanese direct investment, even as many Japanese investors have begun an exodus from China – though some dare to stay,” he said.

He noted that China has not clamped down on financial outflows in yen the way it polices capital flight in US dollars.

“Beijing has taken a selective approach to Japan,” he said.

Is the US still a reliable ally for Japan?

Yes, but not as much as it used to be, experts say.

There are concerns in Japan and among other US allies in Asia, as Washington scales back some military assets in the region to meet its needs in the Middle East, where the US-Israel war on Iran drags on.

Last week, the US moved its last aircraft carrier in Asia from Japan to the Middle East, a move that follows reports earlier this year that the US had moved parts of its Terminal High Altitude Area Defence (THAAD) system from South Korea to use against Iran.

Such moves appear to have emboldened Beijing, with the Chinese fleet moving beyond the First Island Chain, which runs from north of Japan through Taiwan and the northern Philippines to Borneo.

William Yang, senior analyst for Northeast Asia at the International Crisis Group, told Al Jazeera that US redeployments away from the region do dent US power projection in Asia, and its ability to counter threats from China.

However, Taiwanese and Japanese security experts say US interest, along with its aircraft carriers, can be expected to ultimately return to Asia.

Experts say it is too early to tell, but the cross-party delegation of politicians visiting China this week is a good sign.

While there are no high hopes of any substantial outcome, it is a “modest start” to, at the very least, have a dialogue, Loh said.

Matsumura cautioned, however, that politicians who travel to Beijing in what he calls “parliamentarian caucus diplomacy”, “are not necessarily aligned” with the Takaichi administration’s policy lines.

“Nor is the ruling party itself of one mind. Even in the LDP, there is a latent struggle between anti-China/pro-US and pro-China/anti-US,” he said.

In other words, the delegation may say less about where Takaichi stands than about who in Tokyo wants to open a channel, regardless.

Against this historical backdrop, however, Beijing is likely to read any Japanese talk of military force as evidence of a return to wartime militarism, analysts say.

In November last year, Beijing imposed a ban on Japanese seafood following the comments regarding Taiwan by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. Then, in January, it restricted exports of dual-use goods and rare earth minerals for defence or military uses. Dual-use goods include software and technology with potential military or weapons-development applications.

In February, China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) placed 40 Japanese entities under restrictive trade measures relating to dual-use goods. It issued a separate “watch list” of 20 companies for which Chinese exporters must submit individual licence applications, risk assessment reports and written commitments that items will not be used for military or defensive capabilities.
China also issued travel warnings, discouraging its citizens from visiting Japan in an attempt to dent Japan’s vital tourism sector.
According to Shinichi Isa, a politician who has previously served at the Japanese embassy in China, bilateral ties have sunk to their lowest since the 1972 normalisation of relations.
In a post on X earlier this month, he wrote that officials had always remained in communication even during previous lows: “Now all channels between officials and ministries have been cut off.”

Beijing has also noted the severity of the situation, with its Foreign Ministry urging the Japanese government on Friday to take its diplomats’ efforts to repair relations “seriously” and to “take concrete actions” to normalise relations.

Dylan Loh, an associate professor in the Public Policy and Global Affairs programme at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore, told Al Jazeera that bilateral relations “have dropped to their lowest in recent memory; communications have ground to a halt, and there is even more mistrust at both the elite and people-to-people level”.
Can Japan afford to fall out with China?

Chinese arrivals in Japan slumped from 715,700 in October 2025 to 330,000 in December, with visitors from mainland China and Hong Kong normally making up about one-fifth of all visitors, according to a report by the Centre for Strategic and International Studies in February.

However, the report also found that the economic effect was minimal, partly due to a weak yen, as spending by tourists from Taiwan, South Korea, the United States, and Hong Kong offset the decline in Chinese arrivals.
The restrictions on exports of rare earth metals from China are more worrying, however.

China, which supplies about 80 percent of Japan’s rare earth imports, shipped no dysprosium or terbium oxide to Japan between November 2025 and May 2026. These elements are essential for the manufacture of high-performance magnets required for a variety of technological applications, fluorescent lights, and nuclear energy and defence components.
Motor vehicle manufacturers Nissan and Suzuki have reported supply disruptions as a result.

Masahiro Matsumura, professor of international politics and national security at St Andrew’s University in Osaka, told Al Jazeera that the squeeze will eventually be managed, but not quickly. “Over the medium and long run, the impact is likely managed through diversification, including rare earth issues, which is a focal point,” he said.

Japan has diversified the supply of some of these, he said, but still relies on China for others that matter, something he described as a “great headache” for the government and for Japanese high-tech firms.
Elsewhere, Beijing has been more careful.
“Beijing still welcomes Japanese direct investment, even as many Japanese investors have begun an exodus from China – though some dare to stay,” he said.
He noted that China has not clamped down on financial outflows in yen the way it polices capital flight in US dollars.
“Beijing has taken a selective approach to Japan,” he said.
Is the US still a reliable ally for Japan?
Yes, but not as much as it used to be, experts say.

There are concerns in Japan and among other US allies in Asia, as Washington scales back some military assets in the region to meet its needs in the Middle East, where the US-Israel war on Iran drags on.

Last week, the US moved its last aircraft carrier in Asia from Japan to the Middle East, a move that follows reports earlier this year that the US had moved parts of its Terminal High Altitude Area Defence (THAAD) system from South Korea to use against Iran.
Such moves appear to have emboldened Beijing, with the Chinese fleet moving beyond the First Island Chain, which runs from north of Japan through Taiwan and the northern Philippines to Borneo.

William Yang, senior analyst for Northeast Asia at the International Crisis Group, told Al Jazeera that US redeployments away from the region do dent US power projection in Asia, and its ability to counter threats from China.
However, Taiwanese and Japanese security experts say US interest, along with its aircraft carriers, can be expected to ultimately return to Asia.
Experts say it is too early to tell, but the cross-party delegation of politicians visiting China this week is a good sign.
While there are no high hopes of any substantial outcome, it is a “modest start” to, at the very least, have a dialogue, Loh said.

Matsumura cautioned, however, that politicians who travel to Beijing in what he calls “parliamentarian caucus diplomacy”, “are not necessarily aligned” with the Takaichi administration’s policy lines.
“Nor is the ruling party itself of one mind. Even in the LDP, there is a latent struggle between anti-China/pro-US and pro-China/anti-US,” he said.
In other words, the delegation may say less about where Takaichi stands than about who in Tokyo wants to open a channel, regardless.

articles.title: Radiation link in flight attendant's breast cancer, French court finds
articles.summary: Former Air France stewardess Sophie Lainault has had her cancer recognised as an occupational disease.
articles.body:
A French court has for the first time recognised cosmic radiation as a factor in the breast cancer of a long-serving flight attendant.

Sophie Lainault, a 59 year-old former stewardess on Air France, sought to have her cancer recognised as an occupational disease, brought on by conditions at work.

This has now been confirmed in a landmark court ruling in the southwestern town of Bayonne, which said that cosmic radiation was one of three carcinogenic hazards arising from her profession. The other two were passive smoking and prolonged night work.

Smoking was authorised on Air France flights until 2000.

The decision means that Lainault, who is in remission from her cancer, can take early retirement with any further treatment fully reimbursed by the French health system.

And by establishing breast cancer as an officially-recognised risk for flight crews, the court has also cleared the way for many other similar claims, lawyers say.

"My dearest wish is that the decision encourages other women who up until now have not had the courage to take this step," Lainault said.

As stewardess and later purser on Air France airliners, Lainault clocked up 12,600 flight hours between 1989 and 2019. More than half of these were at night.

Many long-distance high-altitude flights from Paris would have taken her near the North Pole, where exposure to radiation from space â strictly speaking particles from the sun and other stars â is the most intense.

A study this month at the Harvard Medical School in the US , external found that flight attendants and pilots had the highest level of radiation-related cancer deaths among more than 500 different professions.

In all, about 6.9% of deaths among flight attendants and 6.7% of deaths among pilots were from radiation-related cancers, according to the analysis.

These proportions were higher than for other professions including nuclear technologists, who are routinely exposed to radiation from non-cosmic sources yet placed 12th on the list, the authors said.

It has long been known that air travel at high altitudes exposes people to cosmic radiation, but the dose for most travellers is regarded as statistically insignificant , external . Exposure at the poles is more intense because elsewhere the earth's magnetic field acts as a shield.

"In France the link between breast cancer and certain hazards has been established for a number of professions, such as nurses â¦ but this is the first time for an air-hostess," said Lainault's lawyer Elisabeth Leroux.

Air France said it had played no part in Lainault's legal case and had not seen the reasoning behind the court's decision.

"The health and security of our staff is an absolute imperative," it said. "Every employee has a medical accompaniment that goes well beyond the regulatory minimum."

articles.title: China’s Xi to visit Kyrgyzstan, Egypt
articles.summary: The Chinese president will attend the SCO summit in Bishkek, before travelling to Egypt.
articles.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping will attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek as part of a state visit to Kyrgyzstan, before travelling to Egypt on a trip from August 30 to September 3, according to Beijing’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

At the SCO summit, to be attended by member states including Russia and Iran, Xi will discuss deepening cooperation as well as major international and regional issues, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian told a daily news conference on Wednesday.

list 1 of 3 How US Senate Russia sanctions could spell 100% tariffs for India, China

list 2 of 3 Can China’s new Arctic sea route to Europe replace Middle East chokepoints?

list 3 of 3 Trump’s Korean gambit exposes a shifting East Asian order

The Chinese president will also hold talks with his Kyrgyz counterpart, Sadyr Japarov, and attend various state events during the trip, he said.

In Egypt, Xi will meet President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi for talks aimed at “making a positive contribution to safeguarding peace and stability in the region”, Lin said.

The state visit, Xi’s first to Egypt in 10 years, “holds special significance for the development of bilateral ties”, Lin added.

The visit comes as Iran and the United States remain locked in a conflict that has spilled over across the Middle East and choked off shipping through the vital Strait of Hormuz, disrupting global oil flows.

China has significant economic ties to the Middle East, which was its top source of crude oil imports before the war.

The tour will be Xi’s second overseas trip this year, following a visit to North Korea in June.

articles.title: Fernando Alonso: Dutch GP strategy shows "I'm a very good driver"
articles.summary: The Aston Martin driver converted a one-stop strategy into a shock points finish
articles.body:
Fernando Alonso was full of self-praise at the Formula 1 Dutch Grand Prix, claiming that being "a very good driver" allowed him to convert a one-stop strategy into a shock points finish for Aston martin

The Spanish racer finished ninth at Zandvoort on Sunday from 18th on the grid, claiming his second points results of the 2026 campaign after 10th at Monaco in June.

The way impressive Alonso took ninth was very impressive too, as he got as far as the 34th lap on a pair of soft tyres before switching to hard rubber for the remainder of the 72-lap contest.

That was amid other drivers utilising at least a two-stop strategy, so the double world champion would wait patiently behind those set to pit and then make the most of the overcut in clean air.

"I'm a very good driver," said Alonso, when asked how he made it work. "That was not the plan. I think the plan was two stops and to go more conventional.

"But we need to sometimes deviate a little bit from what is normal. When we are in traffic, we cannot use our potential.

"We are faster in the corners and the people in front of us, we are slower on the straights, and we're stuck behind.

"So, as soon as we have free track in front of us, we try to use it, even if it's not the optimal performance and the optimal strategy and it's what we did today."

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing, Alexander Albon, Williams

Alonso's result came after Aston Martin brought a radically different chassis to Budapest at the prior round, before bringing an upgraded Honda engine to the Netherlands.

The updates have so far worked well as the British marque is no longer F1's slowest team - a tag that now belongs to newcomer Cadillac - but its Zandvoort weekend didn't start positively.

Alonso qualified last for the sprint race - team-mate Lance Stroll was in 19th - as he encountered driveability problems due to his straightline mode not working, causing him to lock up at Turn 1.

Stroll and the Spaniard eventually finished the sprint in 17th and 18th before a more respectable qualifying session for Sunday's race, taking 18th and 19th ahead of Haas and Cadillac.

Alonso reckons Aston Martin will not be "competitive" at the low-downforce Monza up next, but Zandvoort still represented "another step forward" for the Silverstone-based outfit.

"Especially on the chassis side," he added. "We brought four or five components here.

"Also, the Budapest package was understood in the break and with all the data available after the race, we fine-tuned a little bit the set-up around that new spec, plus the new parts.

"I think, now, we are optimising the chassis side and we are able to extract the maximum.

"On the engine, it's more difficult. I don't think we can be black and white on if we have more power or not.

"From the driver's side of things, you change circuit one month after the other race, so the drivability has been a difficult weekend.

"We're struggling with the downshift again and we're struggling with the engine braking corner to corner. So, it was a challenging weekend in that regard."

How Fernando Alonso scored ninth at Zandvoort - and how Alex Albon lost a similar payday

articles.title: Browns fans are angry at HC Todd Monken over Shedeur Sanders decision for final preseason game
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns QB Shedeur Sanders will not feature in their final preseason game against the New England Patriots, with the third-and-fourth-string QBs get...
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns QB Shedeur Sanders will not feature in their final preseason game against the New England Patriots , with the third-and-fourth-string QBs getting playing time instead.

After a competitive training camp, Sanders lost the QB1 battle to veteran Deshaun Watson for Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars .

With the QB1 battle set, coach Todd Monken's decision not to play Sanders as QB1 for more reps in their final preseason game in favor of giving Dillon Gabriel an opportunity has raised some eyebrows.

Browns HC Todd Monken explains why Dillon Gabriel is playing and Shedeur Sanders isn't

Browns HC Monken spoke to the media on Tuesday after Sanders was confirmed to be out of the rotation for their preseason finale.

"We're not playing them because we'd like to see Dillon (Gabriel) more. It worked out last game, that was unfair to him. So, in order to do that, to see more of him and see Taylen (Green), there's just not enough reps."

"That's the reason, there's really nothing else. Just trying to see Taylen after he played pretty well in the limited reps he had against the Bills, and we want to see more of Dillon. It just hasn't worked out trying to get those other guys reps. That's the reason."

Gabriel started last season ahead of Sanders in the depth chart before losing his role to Sanders amid a rough rookie season. But with Shedeur going from QB3 to QB1 in one season last year, Gabriel could do the same with enough opportunity.

Browns fans are angry at Todd Monken for this decision

Browns fans were not happy to see this, as they would rather see Sanders get more reps than continue with the Gabriel experiment that went badly last season.

"It's like they are doing everything we don't want them to do in succession. Dillon Gabriel shouldn't be on an NFL roster, period," said a concerned fan .

"Cleveland Browns are a joke! Don't want Shedeur to play and completely embarrass them for picking Deshaun Watson over him!" said another fan .

"They want to trade Dillon and he needs more tape. They don't want Shedeur to shine and cause even more uproar over Watson being named," believes one fan .

"He's a clown. Can't wait for our 24th head coach when Monken is fired after this season," said one angry fan .

"That's stunning. Is this real life?" was all one stunned fan could say.

'It's 2016 all over again' – NY Giants fans react to what OBJ has just done in training camp

articles.title: Bayern Munich extends Max Eberl and Jan-Christian Dreesen contracts through 2029
articles.summary: Bayern Munich has extended the contracts of board member for sport Max Eberl and chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen through June 2029.  The Bavarian power...
articles.body:
MUNICH (AP) — Bayern Munich has extended the contracts of board member for sport Max Eberl and chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen through June 2029.

The Bavarian powerhouse announced the extensions after its supervisory board meeting late Tuesday, when it reiterated its faith in Eberl and Dreesen to continue in their roles.

"Our board is ideally positioned to drive FC Bayern forward both in sporting and commercial terms and to maintain its leading position in Europe," the club said.

The 52-year-old Eberl had a challenging start after taking over Bayern's transfer dealings in February 2024 . He endured a long search for a new coach after getting rejections from Xabi Alonso, Julian Nagelsmann and Ralf Rangnick. He then even tried and failed to convince outgoing coach Thomas Tuchel to stay.

Eberl eventually settled on Vincent Kompany , a decision that has proved inspired with the former Manchester City captain leading Bayern to back-to-back Bundesliga titles and a league and cup double last season.

Bayern appointed Dreesen as CEO in May 202 3 after dismissing his predecessor Oliver Kahn . The 58-year-old Dreesen had been vice chairman of the supervisory board since 2014 after joining Bayern as chief financial officer from the banking sector the year before.

articles.title: What’s next for Shedeur Sanders after Deshaun Watson named Browns QB1?
articles.summary: Browns coach Todd Monken said Shedeur Sanders understands 'the long game." What does that look like after Deshaun Watson was named QB1?
articles.body:
The most-talked-about quarterback battle of NFL training camp was settled Monday when Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken announced Deshaun Watson as the team's starting quarterback over Shedeur Sanders .

Watson being named starter is a controversial decision . The embattled quarterback has fallen short of expectations following a record-breaking five-year, $230 million fully guaranteed contract he signed in March of 2022. Still, Monken said Watson gives the Browns the "best chance to move the ball and score points."

The Browns are scheduled to play their final preseason game on Thursday, Aug. 27, against the New England Patriots . Neither Watson nor Sanders is expected to play in Cleveland's preseason finale as they already solidified their roster spots.

Sanders is slated to be No. 2 on the Browns' quarterback depth chart behind Watson. Sanders started seven games as a rookie last year and was even an alternate selection to the Pro Bowl.

Monken told reporters he informed Sanders of the Browns' quarterback decision on Monday and the second-year quarterback handled the news with professionalism.

Shedeur Sanders' journey from college football to Browns quarterback

"He was awesome. You talk about someone that really understands the long game," Monken said. "That really I think that has come to understand the long game. What are we really in this for? What am I in it for? To have the Browns be an organization that people aspire to be, right? The long game. Where do we want to be in the long term?

"He understands that as well as a quarterback. Where he was at, where he's at now (and) where he wants to get to. That is what's so awesome about Shedeur understanding that. We met (Monday) morning for a good long time and all he had was a smile on his face because he understands what's really in front of him. He's gonna work his butt off to get better and he has already."

NANCY ARMOUR: The Browns picked Deshaun Watson over their future. Good luck with that | Opinion

Does Shedeur Sanders still have chance to start for the Browns?

NFL coaches often say it's a week-to-week league. It's often labeled as "coach speak," but there is a lot of truth to those words. Even though Watson was named the Browns starter, his job as QB1 isn't permanent.

The Browns begin the regular season with road games against the Jacksonville Jaguars and Tampa Bay Buccaneers before their home opener against the Carolina Panthers . If the Browns get off to a slow start or Watson performs similarly to his 19 previous career games in Cleveland, Monken could promote Sanders to starter.

It would be logical for the Browns to start Watson to begin the season and then switch to Sanders to finish out the year. It's typically an easier transition to start a veteran quarterback before turning to a younger signal-caller.

It's important for Sanders to stay focused and perform well in practice as he takes No. 2 quarterback reps and continue his development as a QB. There's a good chance his days as a starter in Cleveland are far from over.

"I think Shedeur has done a great job," Monken said. "He's come a long way and we're excited about his future."

articles.title: Jaguars defender puts together disruptive performance in joint practice
articles.summary: One Jaguars' defender put together a highly disruptive day during the team's first joint practice with the Bucs.
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars' defensive end Josh Hines-Allen was extremely disruptive in the team's first joint practice with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

"If Tuesday's practice was a game, Josh Hines-Allen could have set a career-high in single-game sacks," wrote John Shipley of Jaguars on SI.

Mia O'Brien noted that during the one-on-one periods, Hines-Allen won six of his matchups.

That high level of play then carried over to the 11-on-11 work, with O'Brien adding that Hines-Allen had three sacks, including a strip-sack, in just one period.

Along with his pass rush production, Shipley wrote that Hines-Allen was finding success lining up on both sides of the line and in the run game.

Overall, the Jaguars' defense had a strong showing during this first joint practice, and a lot of that success started up front with the play of the defensive line, specifically Hines-Allen.

articles.title: 'OBACHT' with an even clearer design
articles.summary: FC Bayern remains steadfast in its commitment to ensuring a safe, respectful and discrimination-free stadium experience: three years after the launch of ‘OBA...
articles.body:
FC Bayern remains steadfast in its commitment to ensuring a safe, respectful and discrimination-free stadium experience: three years after the launch of 'OBACHT' ('watch out'), the club's awareness concept, the design has now been comprehensively revised and further developed to make it even clearer and easier to understand.

Three years of experience and responsibility

For the past three years, OBACHT has been an integral part of FC Bayern's home matches at the Allianz Arena. During this period, a wealth of experience has been gained, and feedback from fans and experts has been gathered and analysed. These insights have been incorporated into the further development of the concept.

What began as an initiative at the fans' request has since been rolled out to other venues, such as the FC Bayern Campus and BMW Park. It was also adopted by UEFA, the European football governing body, for the 2024 European Championship.

The aim is to foster a strong culture of watching out for one another at all FC Bayern venues and to make attending home matches even safer and more inclusive.

On matchdays, the OBACHT team can also be contacted via the Allianz Arena app.

OBACHT – look out for one another, safeguard one another

In this FC Bayern initiative, the Bavarian term 'OBACHT' stands for looking out for one another, keeping an eye on one another, supporting and respecting one another – and ensuring that qualified help is on hand should anyone need it.

FC Bayern thus recognises that tackling transgressive and discriminatory behaviour must be an ever-present and and indispensable priority. OBACHT raises awareness: looking away is not an option; not looking away is a stance.

Due to its history, its values and its social responsibility, FC Bayern takes a clear and unequivocal stand in favour of diversity, openness and tolerance. To this end, the German champions are committed to taking concrete action and launching initiatives to combat all forms of discrimination, most notably through their ' Red against Racism ' initiative.

Spaces for everyone – at the Arena, BMW Park and the Campus

Everyone should feel comfortable and safe at FC Bayern's match venues and club facilities. The club aims to create spaces for everyone and to foster a culture of being watchful.

OBACHT helps to ensure a safer stadium experience for everyone, irrespective of their background, religion, identity, sexual orientation or gender.

Working with the Südkurve and KIT München

FC Bayern developed OBACHT in collaboration with representatives from the Südkurve München (Munich South Stand) and the Fanprojekt München (Munich fan project), which is run by the non-profit organisation AWO München Stadt ( Munich City Workers' Welfare Association). This close collaboration with the fan community continues: the Südkurve remains an important partner in the further development of the concept to this day, contributing insights and experiences from the stands.

The KIT -München or Munich Crisis Intervention Team, run by the Arbeiter-Samariter-Bund (Workers' Samaritan Foundation), operates as the primary OBACHT team, carrying out awareness-raising work on matchdays, and is not bound by any instructions from the club.

The collaboration with KIT München has been further strengthened through the revised version of OBACHT: processes have been streamlined, responsibilities more clearly defined and the team's visibility to visitors enhanced, not least through the new design and clearer communication materials.

Be watchful together – put OBACHT into practice

OBACHT is more than just a concept on paper or a sign in the Arena: it is lived attitude.

FC Bayern expects all visitors , club members, players, staff and supporters to embody this ethos as part of the club. Together, we can ensure that FC Bayern's venues are places where everyone feels safe and respected.

articles.title: Israel's seizure of Unrwa training college in East Jerusalem condemned
articles.summary: It marks the shutting of the last of the Palestinian refugee agency's facilities in the sector of the city, after Israel passed a law against it.
articles.body:
Israeli security forces have seized and closed a training college run by the UN agency for Palestinian refugees (Unrwa), the last of its facilities that was still operating in occupied East Jerusalem.

UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres has condemned the incursion of the Qalandia Training Centre, the latest move to threaten Unrwa after Israel passed laws against it.

His spokesman, Stephane Dujarric, said that under international law, all UN premises "are inviolable and immune from any form of interference."

Israel's far-right National Security Minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir, joined the large raid on Tuesday and released a video of himself in the chair of the director of the Unrwa institute.

The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he had given the directive for the evacuation of the Unrwa compound, accusing the agency of involvement in the deadly Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, which it strongly denies.

The Qalandia Training Centre, which was set up in 1952, trained some 340 Palestinians a year in valuable vocational skills including carpentry, car mechanics and plumbing.

Although the site is in East Jerusalem, its location between Qalandia and Kfar Aqab is behind Israel's separation barrier, which made it accessible to young people from refugee camps across the West Bank.

Staff have been expelled from the college. The Israeli authorities say equipment is being removed from the site, and they intend to turn part of it into a school.

In a statement, Unrwa said it "unequivocally condemns this unauthorised and deeply concerning incursion into the Qalandia Training Centre".

"The entry of armed security forces into a United Nations facility, without the authorisation or consent of the United Nations, is unacceptable."

Israeli legislation, which came into force last year, banned Unrwa from carrying out missions or operating within what Israel deemed to be its territory. This includes East Jerusalem, which was captured by Israel from Jordan in the 1967 Middle East War and later annexed in a move that is not recognised by most countries.

All Israeli state authorities were also banned from having contact with Unrwa.

Closure orders were issued last year for six Unrwa schools in East Jerusalem, ending in-person teaching for some 800 Palestinian children.

Following the raid on Qalandia Training College, the UN's spokesman said: "The secretary general is greatly alarmed at this development, as it will deprive young people of the vocational education they were receiving."

Israel's security minister made a point of publicising the action, taking a TV crew from pro-government Channel 14 with him for the raid.

"Thank God, on my shift there is no Unrwa, there is no management, they will not be here," Ben-Gvir said in his video at the college.

Moves against Unrwa are broadly popular in Israel and the prime minister put out a statement highlighting his responsibility.

"In accordance with my instructions and in furtherance of the law we passed, the evacuation of the Unrwa compound in Kafr Aqab, Jerusalem, began today," Netanyahu said.

"The State of Israel will not allow an organisation whose employees were involved in terrorism and the October 7 massacre to operate on its territory and will use all means necessary to act against it," he added.

Israeli intelligence claimed that at least 19 Unrwa employees took part in the 7 October cross-border attack on southern Israel, which killed some 1,200 people and led to the abduction of 251 hostages. A UN investigation found that in nine cases the evidence indicated possible involvement, so their contracts were terminated. It found insufficient or no evidence to support claims in the other cases.

Israel further alleged that 10 per cent of Unrwa's Gaza employees had active links to Palestinian armed groups and that Unrwa facilities were used for Hamas military purposes. Unrwa says it has never been given information or evidence from the Israeli authorities about the former allegation and that it has systematically condemned any violations of UN premises which violate their neutrality.

The Palestinian Authority's ministry of foreign affairs called on the international community to "take immediate and effective measures" to protect the college and "ensure the return of its personnel and prevent Israel from turning this assault into a permanent fait accompli".

Unrwa was first set up to support Palestinians who fled or were expelled from their land in fighting before and after the state of Israel was created in 1948.

Many Palestinians see Israeli attacks on the agency as an attempt to dispense with the issue of Palestinian refugees and their "right to return" to their historic homes and property, which is a core issue in the Israel-Palestinian conflict.

articles.title: Cloud seeding drones generate 19 million gallons of water in Alaska in just three hours, raising hopes for drought-hit regions
articles.summary: US News: A Southern California climate-tech start-up says it has produced an estimated 19 million gallons of additional precipitation over Alaskaâs Kenai Penin.
articles.body: A Southern California climate-tech start-up says it has produced an estimated 19 million gallons of additional precipitation over Alaskaâs Kenai Peninsula in just three hours, using drones to seed clouds with silver iodide. The striking claim comes from a research operation conducted by an Alaska based company on 23rd August 2026. The company says its drone-based system could eventually help increase water supplies in drought-stricken parts of the American West, including the Colorado River Basin and the Great Salt Lake. Rather than creating clouds from nothing, the technology targets existing clouds containing supercooled liquid water and encourages the formation of ice crystals that can grow into precipitation. Rainmaker says the Alaska experiment represents an important step towards making cloud seeding more measurable and scalable, although the reported water volume remains a company estimate rather than an independently verified measurement.How Rainmakerâs drone-based cloud seeding system worksRainmaker conducted the operation across seven drone missions, deploying two Elijah autonomous aircraft equipped with silver iodide flares. The drones released 19 flares containing approximately 374 grams of the seeding material into clouds judged to contain suitable atmospheric conditions. Radar observations subsequently identified precipitation signatures associated with the seeded clouds. Rainmakerâs analysis estimated a mean additional precipitation volume of 57.6 acre-feet, equivalent to approximately 19 million gallons of water. The companyâs report placed the estimated range between 45 and 65 acre-feet. Silver iodide served as the ice-nucleating agent, with the experiment targeting supercooled liquid water within the clouds. The findings are significant primarily because the operation attempted to quantify the precipitation response rather than relying solely on observations of rainfall following a seeding flight. Rainmaker has described the Alaska campaign in their validation report as a validation exercise for its drone-based system.Why the Alaska cloud seeding test could matter for drought-hit regionsRainmakerâs Alaska validation report places the experiment within a wider effort to test whether cloud seeding can produce measurable increases in precipitation under naturally occurring conditions. The company identified seven distinct radar signatures during the three-hour operation and estimated that they represented 57.6 acre-feet, or about 71,072 cubic metres, of net new precipitation. Rainmaker notes that glaciogenic cloud seeding is already used across the Colorado River Basin and elsewhere in the American West, with potential applications extending to agricultural, municipal, industrial and environmental water needs, including efforts to restore the Great Salt Lake. The Alaska operation was conducted in an atmosphere that contained ongoing natural precipitation, with soundings showing conditions considered favourable for silver iodide activation. articles.title: Bayer Leverkusen reject Aston Villa transfer approach for Cameroonian striker Christian Kofane
articles.summary: Aston Villa have had an approach rejected for Bayer Leverkusen striker Christian Kofane, according to The Athletic Leverkusen made it clear that they do not...
articles.body:
Aston Villa have had an approach rejected for Bayer Leverkusen striker Christian Kofane, according to The Athletic

Leverkusen made it clear that they do not intend to sell the 20-year-old.

Villa are long-time admirers of Kofane, who joined Leverkusen from Albacete last summer.

His first season in Germany yielded seven goals and nine assists in 44 appearances across all competitions.

His performances earned him a place in Cameroon's squad for the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON), where they reached the quarter-final stage.

Villa are in the market for a potential replacement for Ollie Watkins , who is angling for a move to Saudi Pro League giants Al-Hilal.

They have rejected multiple bids, but Al-Hilal have an agreement with the player on personal terms.

Manager Unai Emery is unwilling to go through the season with Tammy Abraham and Brian Madjo as his options to lead the line.

Chelsea star Nicolas Jackson is also among their targets. He previously played under Emery at Villarreal .

They have had an approach turned down for Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta .

Villa should push the boat out for Jackson

Jackson is the most realistic choice for Villa. He has a respectable record of 24 goals and ten assists in 65 Premier League appearances.

The 25-year-old is familiar with the demands of Premier League football and understands how Emery works.

Kofane and Mateta would not be plug-and-play options for Emery, particularly as they would not have the luxury of pre-season training under him.

Jackson's selfless running and willingness to stretch defences make him the ideal fit for Villa.

With Villa set to compete on four fronts this season, they need a forward who can hit the ground running.

Jackson fits the bill and they must do whatever it takes to sign him before the transfer window closes.

articles.title: Washington Post fired Karen Attiah over social-media posts in 2025; an arbitrator has now ordered her reinstated with full back pay
articles.summary: US News: Karen Attiah, a former Washington Post opinion writer and the newspaper's founding global opinions editor, was fired on September 11, 2025, one day af.
articles.body: Karen Attiah, a former Washington Post opinion writer and the newspaper's founding global opinions editor, was fired on September 11, 2025, one day after conservative activist Charlie Kirk was shot and killed during a public appearance at Utah Valley University. The Post's termination letter accused Attiah of gross misconduct, saying her social-media comments about Kirk's death violated the newspaper's social-media policies, harmed the organisation's integrity and potentially endangered staff. Nearly a year later, independent arbitrator Sarah Miller Espinosa ruled that the Post did not have âgood and sufficient causeâ to terminate Attiah and had violated its collective bargaining agreement with the Washington-Baltimore News Guild. Espinosa ordered the newspaper to reinstate Attiah immediately, with full back pay and lost benefits. The decision is dated August 20, 2026, but was made public four days later, on August 24. The ruling brought a year-long dispute over newsroom discipline and expression to a close.What Karen Attiah posted after Charlie Kirk's killingAttiah made several posts on Bluesky following Kirk's death, discussing political violence and the public reaction to his killing. In one, she wrote that refusing to engage in what she called âperformative mourningâ for âa white man that espoused violenceâ was not itself violence. In another, she criticised what she described as the expectation that people show âcare, empty goodness and absolutionâ toward white men who espouse hatred and violence. Those posts were cited by the Post in the termination letter that ended her employment the following day. At the time, Attiah had spent 11 years at the newspaper, working as both an editor and opinion writer. She focused particularly on race, gender and international human rights and was the last Black full-time member of the Post's opinion desk when she was fired.Why the arbitrator found the Post did not have sufficient cause to fire herThe arbitration hearing took place June 4, 2026. In her ruling, Espinosa found that the Post had failed to establish that Attiah engaged in gross misconduct and had not shown âgood and sufficient causeâ to terminate her employment. The decision concluded that the firing violated the collective bargaining agreement between the newspaper and the Washington-Baltimore News Guild. Espinosa also rejected the Post's interpretation of Attiah's posts as racial or gender-based disparagement. The ruling said it was not reasonable to conclude that the posts referred to or disparaged all white men, or a particular white man, on the basis of race or gender. It also stated that recognising a person's race or gender does not by itself constitute disparagement on those grounds.The ruling noted that Attiah had worked at the Post for 11 years and had not previously been disciplined. Espinosa concluded that the newspaper had not met the standard required under the union agreement to justify termination without progressive discipline. She described the termination penalty as âabsolutely disproportionalâ and ordered the newspaper to reinstate Attiah immediately, with full back pay and lost benefits.What Attiah said after winning the arbitration caseAttiah publicly announced the ruling after the decision became public, saying that an independent arbitrator had ordered the Post to reinstate her with back pay. In a statement, she said the decision confirmed that she had been doing her job as an opinion writer and that doing that job was not misconduct. She added that she was ârelieved to finally have that record set straight.â The Washington-Baltimore News Guild and the Democracy Defenders Fund, which supported her case, welcomed the ruling as a significant victory for the union and press freedom. The Washington Post said it respects the arbitration process and declined to comment further on the ruling.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
